guides.name: Apple
guides.summary: Legacy Contact, data access and closure
prepareSteps: Open Settings → your name → Sign-In & Security → Legacy Contact.
Add the person, then share or print their access key.
Confirm they received the key and keep its location with your estate documents.
laterSteps: Look for the Legacy Contact access key. If available, open Apple Digital Legacy using the official link below.
Provide the key and death certificate or regional equivalent. Follow Apple’s document review.
Without an access key, use Apple’s family-member route for country-specific legal-document instructions.
Follow Apple’s approved access or deletion route. Do not erase a device before considering whether needed data would be lost.
usuallyRequested: Legacy Contact access key, if available
Legal authority or court documents if Apple requests them
guides.boundary: Legacy Contact excludes Keychain passwords, passkeys, payment data and purchased media. Other access requests depend on local documentation; approval is not guaranteed.

links.title: No access key or need account closure?

guides.name: Google
guides.summary: Inactive Account Manager and family requests
prepareSteps: Open Google Inactive Account Manager while signed in to your own account.
Choose the inactivity period, up to ten contacts and the data each may receive.
Choose whether to delete the account afterward, and keep contact details current.
laterSteps: Open Google’s deceased-user request form and choose closure, funds or account content.
If content is needed, request it first. Closing the account prevents a later content request.
Provide the identity, death and authority evidence Google requests through its form. Wait for its review.
usuallyRequested: Death and relationship or authority evidence
guides.boundary: Inactivity is not proof of death. Google never gives out passwords, and every deceased-user request is reviewed.

guides.name: Microsoft
guides.summary: Outlook and OneDrive access depends on region and law.
prepareSteps: Record the account identifier and billing locator; Microsoft does not publish a consumer Legacy Contact setting.
laterSteps: Use Microsoft’s deceased-account instructions for the account region.
Expect a court-order route for content in many regions; China and Germany have documented alternatives.
usuallyRequested: Court order or region-specific authority documents
guides.boundary: A request does not guarantee account content. Requirements vary materially by region.

guides.name: Dropbox
guides.summary: Request access to a deceased person’s files
prepareSteps: Record the account email and the location of any locally synced Dropbox folder.
laterSteps: If legally permitted, check the local Dropbox folder for existing copies. Otherwise request access from Dropbox.
Create a support ticket with the deceased person’s name/email, your contact details, relationship, government ID and the court order specified by Dropbox.
Wait for Dropbox’s review before assuming access is available.
usuallyRequested: Deceased person’s name and account email
Requestor contact, relationship and government ID
Court order meeting Dropbox’s stated requirements
guides.boundary: Dropbox requires proof of death and lawful access. Providing documents does not guarantee access.

guides.name: Yahoo
guides.summary: Regional closure, billing and content options
prepareSteps: Record the Yahoo ID and account region. Save important material while you are authorized to do so.
laterSteps: Choose the official Yahoo page for the account’s region before submitting anything.
For U.S. accounts, choose closure, billing cancellation or a content request; each has its own form and requirements.
Outside the U.S., follow regional guidance. The global page requests a closure letter, executor/representative appointment and death certificate.
usuallyRequested: Executor appointment; U.S. content requests additionally need ID and a qualifying U.S. court order
guides.boundary: Yahoo does not provide passwords. Account and content-access rules depend on region; U.S. forms reject non-U.S. accounts.

guides.name: Facebook
prepareSteps: In Facebook Accounts Centre, open Personal details → Account ownership and control → Memorialisation.
Choose a Legacy Contact or Delete after death. Decide whether permitted content downloads should be allowed.
laterSteps: Use Facebook’s deceased-account help to request memorialization or removal.
For removal, follow the proof-of-death and family or estate-authority requirements. Do not sign in as the deceased person.
usuallyRequested: Relationship or estate authority for removal
guides.boundary: A Legacy Contact cannot log in or read private messages. Memorialization and removal do not transfer account ownership.

guides.name: Instagram
prepareSteps: Record the profile URL and whether you prefer memorialization or removal.
laterSteps: Open Instagram’s deceased-account guidance and select memorialization or removal.
Submit the proof of death requested; removal additionally requires an authorized family member or representative.
usuallyRequested: Family relationship or estate authority for removal
guides.boundary: Instagram does not provide another person’s login or a Facebook-style Legacy Contact setting.

guides.name: LinkedIn
guides.summary: Memorialize the profile or request closure with authority.
prepareSteps: Record the profile URL, account email and preferred memorialize-or-close outcome.
laterSteps: Report the death for memorialization, or request closure if legally authorized.
Provide the profile URL, relationship and death information. For closure, include LinkedIn-accepted court documents appointing the estate representative.
guides.boundary: LinkedIn never provides usernames or passwords. Memorialization locks access.

guides.name: X
guides.summary: An estate representative or close family member can request deactivation.
prepareSteps: Record the handle, profile URL and preferred outcome; do not plan around another person receiving access.
laterSteps: Submit X’s removal request, then follow the emailed identity and death-certificate instructions.
usuallyRequested: Estate authority or verified family relationship
guides.boundary: X’s published route deactivates the account. It does not give another person account access.

links.title: Contact X about a deceased user

guides.name: PayPal
guides.summary: An executor can request closure and balance handling.
prepareSteps: Record the primary email and exact PayPal country/entity without storing a payment credential.
laterSteps: Check the PayPal country/entity. The U.S. guide below is for an authorized executor or administrator.
Follow the official regional submission instructions with the account email, death certificate, requestor ID and estate authority. The U.S. process also requests an estate W-9.
Ask PayPal to review closure and the permitted balance-disbursement option. Do not change account ownership or sign in as the deceased.
usuallyRequested: Requestor contact details and closure request
Death certificate and requestor photo ID
Estate W-9 for the U.S. process
guides.boundary: Requirements and balance options vary by PayPal entity and country. Do not impersonate the account holder.

guides.name: Coinbase
guides.summary: Use Executor Services; individual accounts do not name a beneficiary.
prepareSteps: Record the account email and cover the custodial assets in estate documents; never store password, 2FA or wallet seed.
laterSteps: The claimant uses their own Coinbase account and opens Executor Services.
Upload the death, probate, ID and signed transfer instructions requested by Coinbase.
Complete the Executor Services form, generate its verification code and follow the official verification instructions for case support.
guides.boundary: Estate documents or applicable succession law determine ownership; Coinbase reviews and transfers custodial assets.

guides.name: Binance
prepareSteps: Record the exact Binance entity and the account’s email, phone or Binance ID.
Keep custody and estate documents identifiable. Do not record passwords, 2FA secrets or wallet seeds.
laterSteps: Use your own Binance account. Open Customer Support → Self Service → View All → Account → Legacy Inheritance.
Identify the deceased person using their email, phone number or Binance ID. Submit the legally valid inheritance documents requested by the form.
Wait for Binance’s review and follow the approved beneficiary or trustee transfer process. If the account is Binance.US, use its separate guide.
usuallyRequested: Deceased user email, phone or Binance ID
Legally valid inheritance documents requested for that entity
guides.boundary: This is an after-death claim reviewed by Binance, not a preselected Legacy Contact or permission to use another person’s login. Entity and local-law requirements vary.

guides.name: Binance.US
prepareSteps: Record that this is Binance.US, with a safe account locator and estate-document location.
laterSteps: Open Binance.US’s deceased-user instructions and contact its support team.
Provide its required selfie video, death certificate, claimant ID and will or probate documents through official support.
Follow the team’s reviewed transfer instructions. Do not use the Binance.com form for this account.
usuallyRequested: Selfie video stating preferred asset transfer
Will and/or probate or estate appointment
guides.boundary: This document list is specific to Binance.US. It does not recover self-custody wallets or establish inheritance rights by itself.

guides.name: GitHub
guides.summary: Invite a repository successor before access is needed.
prepareSteps: Open Settings › Account › Successor settings.
Invite another GitHub user and confirm they accepted.
laterSteps: The successor or authorized person contacts GitHub Support and states the requested action.
Provide the username, relationship and requested identity, death or authority documents.
guides.boundary: A successor cannot sign in as the user and can manage only the public user-owned repository scope described by GitHub.

guides.name: Bitwarden & 1Password
prepareSteps: For Bitwarden, check Premium or paid-organization eligibility, choose view or takeover access and a wait period, then invite a contact on the same Bitwarden server. They accept; you confirm.
For 1Password Families, add another organizer, save the Emergency Kit and generate a recovery code.
laterSteps: The confirmed Bitwarden contact requests Emergency Access from their own account. Access follows approval or the configured wait; it does not establish inheritance.
For 1Password, follow the family’s prearranged lawful plan. Organizer recovery requires the member’s email step and is not a deceased-account transfer service.
guides.boundary: Emergency access can expose highly sensitive vault data and does not create legal authority. Never store a vault master password, Secret Key or recovery code in Rillora.

guides.name: Adobe
guides.summary: Cancel subscriptions or close an account
prepareSteps: Record the Adobe ID email and active subscriptions; keep needed files in an authorized location.
laterSteps: Open Adobe’s official instructions, then its privacy inquiry form. Verify your own contact email.
Choose the request for another person’s death, enter their Adobe ID, and provide the requested legal documentation.
Submit the request as the authorized representative and retain Adobe’s response.
usuallyRequested: Death certificate and authority documentation as requested
guides.boundary: This route concerns closure or cancellation. It does not promise transfer of an Adobe account, software license or cloud files.

guides.name: Netflix
prepareSteps: Record the account email or phone and where its subscription is billed.
laterSteps: Open Netflix’s deceased-member page and use the no-account-access support route.
Contact Netflix with the account email or phone. Provide any required billing information only through Netflix’s official support channel.
Request cancellation and keep its confirmation. Do not obtain or use the deceased person’s password.
usuallyRequested: Billing information requested directly by Netflix
guides.boundary: This is subscription cancellation, not account inheritance. Never store payment credentials in Rillora.

guides.name: Steam
prepareSteps: Record the Steam profile or account locator. Do not treat the game library as an automatically transferable account.
laterSteps: Read the Steam Subscriber Agreement’s account-transfer restrictions.
Ask Steam Support what lawful options and documents apply to the estate; do not share the deceased person’s login.
usuallyRequested: Requestor contact and only documents Steam asks for
guides.boundary: Steam accounts and subscriptions are personal and generally non-transferable unless Valve permits otherwise. No dedicated estate-transfer workflow is claimed here.
